Panel sizes and margins in a layout

Source: R/size.R
auto_width.Rd

A plot often has more space in a layout than its panel needs, e.g. a plot below a row of plots, or next to a taller plot. These functions decide how a plot uses that space:

Usage

auto_width(...)

auto_height(...)

auto_margins(..., x = TRUE, y = TRUE)

set_size(..., width = NULL, height = NULL)

Arguments

...

ggplots, layouts, or lists of them.

x, y

Center horizontally / vertically.

width, height

Panel width and height in mm. NULL leaves a dimension unchanged.

Value

The modified plot or layout if one object was supplied, otherwise a list. Layout functions such as new_row() splice such lists, so new_column(auto_height(p1, p2)) works.

Details

  • auto_width() and auto_height() let the layout decide the panel size: the panel takes exactly the space the plot gets from its neighbours. It can become larger or smaller than before.

  • auto_margins() keeps the panel at its size and centers the plot in the spare space, with equal room on both sides (like margin: auto in CSS). The tag stays at the edge of the space. Only spare space within the row, column or grid the plot sits in is used. Centering vertically (y = TRUE) moves the plot away from the row's shared bottom edge, so its x axis no longer lines up with its neighbours'.

  • set_size() sets a fixed panel size in mm. For tidyplots it calls tidyplots::adjust_size(); for plain ggplots it sets theme(panel.widths, panel.heights), always per panel (also for facets).

If several plots in a row or column take spare space, they share it equally. These functions work for tidyplots and plain ggplots. Layouts are modified recursively, i.e. all plots inside them are changed.

Examples

p1 <- dummy(name = "p1", color = "#0072B2")
p2 <- dummy(name = "p2", color = "#D55E00")
p3 <- dummy(name = "p3", color = "#009E73")
wide <- dummy(name = "wide", color = "#E69F00", width = 50)

new_column(p1, p2) |>
  new_column(auto_height(p3))


new_row(p1, p2) |>
  new_row(auto_width(p3))


# keep the panel size, center the plot in the spare width
new_row(wide, wide) |>
  new_row(p1, auto_margins(p2, y = FALSE)) |>
  layout_tags("A")


new_row(p1, set_size(p2, width = 45))
